To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we propose an enhanced time-varying single-carrier channel estimation based on the combination of DDST and bi-dimensional basis expansion.
we propose a novel technique that enhances the channel estimation based on superimposing training and self-interference cancellation.
the combination of a two-dimensional basis expansion and a data-dependent superimposing scheme allows to improve channel estimation in the presence of a large number of users.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a new approach for channel estimation based on the combination of DDST with a bi-dimensional projection of the channel impulse response onto an orthonormal basis.
a new approach for channel estimation in the case of ST, where the use of the basis expansion is proposed.

the development of new techniques for the enhancement of time-varying single carrier channel estimation, which can be used in a wide range of applications, including cognitive radio, where the channel is unknown and the bandwidth is scarce.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, by using the proposed method, the channel estimation error can be reduced in the range of 1 dB with respect to the best existing techniques.

the proposed method outperforms the state of the art techniques, and that this is a consequence of the use of the bi-dimensional projection of a basis function, the suppression of self-interference, and the use of a more robust channel estimator.

the proposed method offers a significant improvement in terms of mean square error (MSE) in the estimation of the channel coefficients, with respect to the conventional ST method, as well as to the DDST method.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have proposed a novel channel estimation scheme for single-carrier communication systems, based on DDST and bi-dimensional basis expansion, which is capable of achieving a better performance in comparison with other techniques.
, by using the DDST, the performance is enhanced by means of the use of a bi-dimensional basis projection.
the proposed method allows the estimation of the channel with the minimum possible overhead, and it can be applied in any type of wireless communication system.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a bi-dimensional basis projection can be used in order to improve the estimation of the time-varying single-carrier communication channel.
a better performance can be achieved with a lower computational cost, and with a lower number of transmitted symbols.
, by means of DDST, we can obtain a channel estimation with a better trade-off between the estimation mean square error and the computational cost.
